scenario: My manager moved our weekly one-on-one into a shared slot with two colleagues without telling me, and she has stopped commenting on my drafts. Last week she praised a teammate's report in the group chat.
reading1: she is deliberately making me more independent because she is preparing me for a bigger role
reading2: she is simply overloaded and restructuring her calendar for reasons that have nothing to do with me
reading3: she is losing confidence in my work and is quietly distancing herself from me

scenario: A colleague who joined after me was invited to present to a client, using slides I built. I only found out the day before, from someone else.
reading1: it was a last-minute scheduling accident and nobody thought about who should attend
reading2: my manager thinks the colleague is better suited to client-facing work than I am
reading3: my manager wants to shield me from client pressure while I am still learning

scenario: A senior partner asked for my opinion in front of the whole team. After I answered, he nodded and moved straight to the next agenda item without any reaction.
reading1: he disagreed with my answer but chose not to argue with me in public
reading2: he was already focused on the next item and did not register my answer much either way
reading3: he valued my answer and is still thinking about it

scenario: HR booked a 'career conversation' with me for next week. The invite has no agenda, and my manager said only that it is 'a good thing to have'.
reading1: it is a routine check-in that every employee gets at this time of year
reading2: I am being considered for a promotion or a new role
reading3: the company is planning a restructuring and wants to know my intentions

scenario: Since our startup closed its funding round, the founder has stopped inviting me to the weekly leadership sync. He is still friendly and keeps asking how my work is going.
reading1: he is sparing me from meetings that have become mostly about investors and finance
reading2: roles are being formalised and I am not part of the new leadership tier
reading3: the meeting simply shrank to fewer people for efficiency and my absence is incidental

scenario: A recruiter offered me a job at a higher salary but wants an answer within 48 hours. When I asked about my future team, he gave only general answers.
reading1: the recruiter genuinely does not know the team details because the team is still being formed
reading2: the role is being filled in haste because people keep leaving the team
reading3: the team is a strong one and the recruiter is just in a hurry to close

scenario: Three weeks ago I asked to work remotely two days a week. My manager said 'let me see what I can do' and has not mentioned it since.
reading1: she has simply forgotten amid a very busy period
reading2: she is reluctant and is hoping I will let the request drop
reading3: she is lobbying for me behind the scenes and waiting on an approval

scenario: A peer was selected for the company's 'high potential' programme. I meet every criterion on the published list and was not nominated, and my manager has not explained.
reading1: nominations were capped per team and it came down to timing rather than merit
reading2: my manager plans to nominate me in the next cycle and thought I could wait
reading3: she has a concern about my performance that is not on the published criteria

scenario: My team lead has started copying her own boss on every email she sends me. Nothing in the content has changed, and she is as friendly as before.
reading1: she is deliberately raising my visibility with her boss
reading2: her boss asked her to copy him on everything, for the whole team, and it is not about me
reading3: she is building a paper trail about my work in case there is a performance issue

scenario: My annual review came back 'meets expectations' after 'exceeds' last year. My manager said it was 'a tougher calibration year' and offered no other detail.
reading1: calibration really was stricter for everyone and my performance has not changed
reading2: a company-wide limit on top ratings forced the result and it says nothing about my work
reading3: my performance slipped and she is softening the message

scenario: A recruiter from a competitor messaged me twice after I posted about a project I led. The messages are friendly but vague about the actual role.
reading1: it is template outreach sent to everyone in my field
reading2: they genuinely want to hire me for the skills shown in that project
reading3: the competitor is targeting my team to weaken it, and I am just one of several approached

scenario: My manager asked me to 'document everything you know' about the systems I run, due by the end of this week, without saying why.
reading1: she is preparing for her own leave or an audit and needs documentation from everyone
reading2: I am being prepared for a move to a new project and need to hand over
reading3: the company is considering replacing me or cutting my role

scenario: My co-founder moved to another city a month ago without discussing it. He replies to messages more slowly now and has missed two of our weekly calls.
reading1: he is building another venture on the side and is losing focus on ours
reading2: he is dealing with a family matter and does not want to burden me with it
reading3: he is burned out and needs space but does not know how to say so

scenario: After my presentation to the director, she said 'interesting, let's take this offline'. A week later nothing has been scheduled.
reading1: it is a stock phrase she says often and she will not follow up unless reminded
reading2: she disagreed and used the phrase to close the topic politely
reading3: she was impressed and wants a private deep dive when her schedule allows

scenario: I was asked to train a new hire who has the same title as me and will report to the same manager. My manager called it 'a great responsibility'.
reading1: I am being groomed to lead the team
reading2: the new hire is meant to take over part of my work in time
reading3: my manager simply needs someone who knows the processes to onboard the newcomer

scenario: My internship supervisor praised my work warmly in person but, when I asked for a written recommendation, said 'just ask me later'.
reading1: company policy limits what supervisors can put in writing and she is awkward about saying it
reading2: she is not confident enough in my work to put her name on a recommendation
reading3: she is swamped and will happily write it when she has time

scenario: A client who used to praise my work has begun sending every question to my manager instead of me, although the project is unchanged.
reading1: the client's own boss now requires them to deal with managers only
reading2: the client is unhappy with something I did and has lost trust
reading3: the client sees my manager as the right person for bigger decisions as the project grows

scenario: The mid-year raise announcement did not arrive this year, and my colleagues have not heard anything either. Nobody in management has mentioned it.
reading1: the announcement was postponed for administrative reasons and everyone will get it soon
reading2: the company is delaying raises because of budget concerns
reading3: raises were decided individually and I was not selected

scenario: I applied for a role on another team. The hiring manager interviewed me, and since then my current manager has seemed cooler and shorter with me.
reading1: her mood is caused by pressure from something else entirely and is unrelated to my application
reading2: she is worried about losing me and is trying to give me space to decide
reading3: she feels betrayed that I might leave

scenario: My PhD supervisor has not answered my emails for two weeks, just before a conference submission deadline. Her calendar shows her as in the office.
reading1: she is travelling or on leave and I missed an announcement about it
reading2: she is unhappy with my progress and is avoiding the conversation
reading3: she is buried in her own grant deadlines and will answer when she can

scenario: My equity paperwork shows a vesting cliff date different from the one my manager described when I joined. Nobody has acknowledged the difference.
reading1: the terms were changed deliberately and not communicated to me
reading2: it is a clerical error that will be corrected when I raise it
reading3: I misremember the verbal terms and the document is right

scenario: A senior colleague is warm and friendly with me but never includes me in the hallway conversations where decisions seem to get made.
reading1: he is deliberately keeping me out of informal decision-making
reading2: he only includes people through formal invitations and treats everyone the same way
reading3: he does not think of me because I am newer

scenario: At the all-hands I asked the CEO a pointed question. She said 'great question, let's talk after', and later I received a meeting invite from the COO's assistant.
reading1: they want to involve me in the initiative I asked about
reading2: it is just routine escalation to whoever owns the topic
reading3: my question touched a sensitive subject and they want to manage me

scenario: A project I worked on failed to launch. Nobody has mentioned it since, and my manager is being unusually nice to me.
reading1: she feels guilty because she knows the blame will fall on me later
reading2: she is being supportive and does not blame me
reading3: the postmortem has simply been delayed and her kindness is her normal manner

scenario: A freelance client paid me late twice and now asks for extra work at the same rate, calling it 'a trial of a longer relationship'.
reading1: they are testing how much I will accept before pushing back
reading2: they genuinely plan a long-term engagement and are cautious about spending
reading3: they have cash-flow problems and are stretching me to cope

scenario: I was moved to a desk far from the rest of my team 'temporarily because of space'. Nobody has said when I will move back.
reading1: someone wants me away from the team because of a conflict
reading2: it is a quiet first step toward moving me to a different team
reading3: office space really is tight and this is purely logistical

scenario: During a casual coffee chat my manager asked me where I see myself in five years. She wrote nothing down and changed the subject quickly.
reading1: she is worried I will leave and is checking my loyalty
reading2: she is considering me for a larger role and wants to know my ambitions
reading3: she was just making conversation

scenario: An idea I proposed in a team meeting appeared in a manager's slide deck for senior leadership, without my name on it.
reading1: she thinks ideas from the team belong to the team and does not attribute individuals
reading2: she is deliberately taking credit for it
reading3: it was an oversight and she will correct it when told

scenario: A fellowship coordinator replied to my inquiry with 'we'll be in touch', and I have heard nothing for three weeks while others in my cohort have received updates.
reading1: I was not selected and they are avoiding the rejection email
reading2: decisions are delayed by a committee and no one has heard yet
reading3: my email or their reply ended up lost in a spam folder or a mix-up

scenario: My manager offered me a stretch project with 'no extra pay, but great visibility' on top of my normal workload.
reading1: the company is trying to get extra work out of me for free
reading2: she has no budget to offer anything more and truly believes the visibility will help me
reading3: it is genuinely a route to promotion and she wants to push me forward

scenario: My new employer asked for my previous manager's contact details for a reference check, and has gone quiet for ten days since.
reading1: the role has been put on hold for reasons unrelated to me
reading2: my previous manager said something negative
reading3: the reference check is routine and still in progress

scenario: A new VP has arrived and morale on my team has dropped. His office has invited me, individually, for coffee.
reading1: he is considering me for a bigger role
reading2: he wants candid information about the team from me
reading3: he is meeting every person on the team one by one as part of his introductions

scenario: My manager asked me to move from engineering to product 'for a few months'. She was vague about what happens afterwards.
reading1: she needs temporary cover and will move me back when it is done
reading2: my engineering role is being phased out
reading3: it is a growth opportunity she wants me to have

scenario: A mentor of mine suggested, out of the blue, that I 'start looking around' for other opportunities. He gave no reason when I asked.
reading1: he senses layoffs coming and is trying to protect me
reading2: he thinks my manager is holding me back
reading3: he thinks I have outgrown my current company

scenario: After I gave notice, my boss said he would 'make it worth my while to stay', but a week later he has not mentioned it again.
reading1: he said it reflexively and has no authority to deliver anything
reading2: he is annoyed that I am leaving and has stopped trying
reading3: he is arranging a counter-offer and needs approval first

scenario: A coworker keeps asking me, casually and in different ways, what I earn. She is otherwise friendly and professional.
reading1: she plans to use my number as leverage in a negotiation
reading2: she is curious and does not realise it is a sensitive question
reading3: she is benchmarking her own pay and wants to know whether she is underpaid

scenario: My team leader was recently promoted. He now answers my messages with one word and no longer asks for my input on planning, though we used to talk daily.
reading1: the promotion has overloaded him and it is not personal
reading2: he is unhappy with something I did and has not said so
reading3: he wants to put professional distance between himself and former peers

scenario: A close friend has cancelled our plans twice this month at the last minute. She still sends me memes and likes my posts, and she posted photos from a dinner with others last weekend.
reading1: she is going through something private and is withdrawing from everyone, including me
reading2: she has quietly started prioritising other friends over me
reading3: she is simply overscheduled and the cancellations are about logistics, not about me

scenario: My partner started leaving the room to take phone calls, and he now keeps his phone face down on the table. Otherwise he seems normal and affectionate.
reading1: he is hiding something from me that would hurt our relationship
reading2: he is dealing with a stressful matter, such as family or work, and does not want to worry me
reading3: he is planning a surprise for me

scenario: My younger sister, who used to send long messages, now replies with a single word. When I called, she said she was 'fine, just busy'.
reading1: she really is just busy with exams or work and it has nothing to do with our relationship
reading2: she is struggling with something in her own life and does not want to talk about it
reading3: she is upset with me about something I did and has not said it

scenario: My roommate has been unusually quiet for a week and spends most of the time in her room with the door closed. She still says hello and has not complained about anything.
reading1: she is annoyed with me about the apartment and is avoiding a confrontation
reading2: she is stressed or low for reasons unrelated to our flat
reading3: she is deep in a study or work crunch and is protecting her time

scenario: The group chat I'm in has gone quiet since I shared my opinion about a mutual friend's wedding plans. Two friends have mentioned 'the other chat' in passing.
reading1: the group is just quiet for a few days and the other chat has nothing to do with me
reading2: my comment offended someone and people are avoiding the subject around me
reading3: the wedding party set up a separate planning chat and I am not part of it by design

scenario: My mother phoned me three times this week asking if I'm 'eating properly' and 'sleeping enough', although I told her nothing about my health.
reading1: she is worried about me because she senses something I have not told her
reading2: she is anxious about something in her own life and is projecting it onto me
reading3: she is just being herself, because it is her usual way of showing care

scenario: A friend I've known for ten years did not invite me to his birthday dinner, though everyone else in our group went. He messaged me afterwards, 'sorry we missed you'.
reading1: he deliberately left me out because of tension between us
reading2: he assumed I was busy or out of town and did not want to put me on the spot
reading3: it was a small gathering that grew by word of mouth and he did not plan to exclude me

scenario: My partner said 'we should talk about the future' and then did not bring it up again for three days, though he seems nervous around me.
reading1: he is considering ending the relationship
reading2: he wants to discuss a practical matter such as a job relocation or finances
reading3: he wants to talk about moving in or getting engaged

scenario: My flatmate's boyfriend has started staying over most nights. He is friendly, but I now feel tense in my own home.
reading1: I am being territorial and my reaction is more about me than about him
reading2: my flatmate has changed our living arrangement without asking me and I have a fair grievance
reading3: I am more tired than usual and my tension comes from sleep and stress, not from them

scenario: My best friend congratulated me on my promotion with a thumbs-up emoji and nothing else, though she usually writes long messages.
reading1: she was typing quickly between tasks and meant nothing by it
reading2: she is overwhelmed with her own problems and has little energy to spare
reading3: she is envious and finding it hard to be happy for me

scenario: I lent my cousin money last spring. He has been avoiding my calls and was seen at an expensive restaurant, although he said he was 'broke'.
reading1: he has no intention of repaying me
reading2: he is being treated by someone else and his finances are the same as he described
reading3: he is ashamed that he cannot repay and is avoiding me out of embarrassment

scenario: My partner's best friend has begun sending me messages that are slightly too personal, like asking about my day in detail and commenting on my photos.
reading1: he has romantic interest in me
reading2: this is simply how he communicates with everyone, and I am reading too much into it
reading3: he is trying to befriend me because I matter to my partner

scenario: After a heated argument last month, my brother and I have not spoken. Yesterday he sent me a link to an article about a topic we both like, with no comment.
reading1: it is his way of reaching out and he hopes I will respond
reading2: he is acting as if nothing happened to avoid the conversation about the argument
reading3: he sent it automatically as he would any friend and it carries no message

scenario: My neighbour, who always chats, has stopped greeting me and crosses the road when she sees me. I cannot think of anything I did.
reading1: she has not noticed me and I am reading too much into a coincidence
reading2: she is going through something personal and is avoiding everyone
reading3: she is upset about something she believes I did, such as noise or parking

scenario: My closest friend recently got a new group of friends from her gym. She still texts me, but her messages are shorter and she mentions 'the gang' a lot.
reading1: she is enjoying a new phase and our friendship is fine
reading2: she is drifting away from me and our friendship is fading
reading3: she wants to include me and is waiting for me to join them

scenario: My partner's parents were polite but very quiet at dinner with us last night. Afterward my partner said 'they just need time', without elaborating.
reading1: they are uncomfortable with me and have reservations about the relationship
reading2: they are worried about something unrelated, such as health or money
reading3: they are naturally reserved and this is how they act with all new people

scenario: A friend asked to 'borrow' my notes and presentation slides for a course we are both enrolled in. She has previously done the same for others, and she was very enthusiastic when I agreed.
reading1: she is relying on my work to avoid doing her own
reading2: she is just collecting material from several people as a study habit
reading3: she is struggling and genuinely needs help

scenario: My friend keeps changing the subject when I ask about her new relationship. She used to share everything.
reading1: she is keeping it private because it is new and fragile, and it says nothing about us
reading2: she is unsure about the relationship and does not want to talk about it yet
reading3: she is worried I will judge her partner or her choices

scenario: My father, who rarely texts, sent me a message saying 'call me when you can, nothing urgent'. It has been two days and I have not called.
reading1: he wants to ask a practical favour or discuss a small family matter
reading2: he has something difficult to tell me, such as a health issue
reading3: he wants to share good news or make plans

scenario: A close friend lent me a book months ago and has not asked for it back, but yesterday she asked whether I 'still had it' without further comment.
reading1: she needs the book back and is hinting
reading2: she was just making conversation and has no particular reason
reading3: she is checking whether I valued her gift, because she is hurt that I have not mentioned it

scenario: My partner keeps saying 'it's fine' when I ask whether something is bothering him. His tone is flat and he has been spending more time with friends.
reading1: something I did is bothering him and he is avoiding the conversation
reading2: he really is fine and is in a quieter phase
reading3: he is stressed about work or family and does not want to talk about it

scenario: My college roommate, whom I haven't seen in years, suddenly messaged to say she is 'in my city next month and would love to catch up'.
reading1: she wants something from me, like a place to stay or a favour
reading2: she is simply passing through and is reaching out to many old contacts
reading3: she wants to rekindle the friendship

scenario: I found out that a friend discussed something I had told her in confidence with another friend. She has not mentioned it to me.
reading1: she did it carelessly and does not realise it was a problem
reading2: the information reached the other friend through someone else, and she did not break my confidence
reading3: she did it deliberately because she thought she was helping

scenario: My boyfriend's ex has liked several of my photos in the last week. We have never spoken.
reading1: she is curious about me and is keeping an eye on the relationship
reading2: she follows many people and it is meaningless
reading3: she is trying to signal friendliness and move on peacefully

scenario: When I told my parents I plan to move abroad for a job, my father said 'we'll see' and my mother changed the subject. Nobody has brought it up since.
reading1: they need time to absorb it and will raise it when they are ready
reading2: they are afraid of missing me and are not ready to talk about it
reading3: they disapprove and hope I will drop the idea

scenario: My friend of many years has begun saying 'we should do this again soon!' at the end of every meetup, but she has not initiated one in months.
reading1: she is waiting for me to suggest something, as I used to
reading2: she wants less contact and is using politeness to soften it
reading3: she values our friendship but is bad at planning

scenario: My partner suggested separate holidays this year 'to have some space', and presented it as a casual idea.
reading1: he wants to do something specific, like a trip with friends, that I would not enjoy
reading2: he needs time alone and it is a healthy request
reading3: he is unhappy in the relationship and testing independence

scenario: My housemate cooked dinner for everyone for the first time ever and asked me to 'tell the others how nice it was'.
reading1: she is proud of her cooking and wants some encouragement
reading2: she is about to ask for something, like a change in the chores or a favour
reading3: she wants to improve her standing in the house after a recent tension

scenario: My teenage cousin, who usually talks to me about everything, has begun giving me polite, short answers and spending time on her phone around me.
reading1: she is going through normal teenage withdrawal from family
reading2: she is upset with me about something I said
reading3: she has a secret she does not want to share, such as a relationship

scenario: A friend I helped through a hard time hasn't contacted me for two months, even though I have messaged her. Her other friends say she is 'doing great'.
reading1: she is embarrassed about having needed help and is avoiding me
reading2: she is busy rebuilding her life and will reach out when she is ready
reading3: she has moved on and our friendship was tied to the hard period

scenario: My wife has begun reorganising our home and said 'I just feel like a change'. She has also been quieter over meals.
reading1: she is stressed or unhappy about something else and is channelling it into the house
reading2: she wants a fresh start in our relationship and is signalling it
reading3: she wants a change in the house and nothing more

scenario: My friend told me that someone from our circle 'said something about me' but refused to say who or what. I have been uneasy since.
reading1: she misunderstood a joke and there is nothing to worry about
reading2: there is a real, hurtful comment and she is protecting me from details
reading3: she is exaggerating a trivial remark for drama

scenario: My brother-in-law has started calling me more often and asking about my work, although we had hardly spoken before.
reading1: he is going through a hard time and reaching out for company
reading2: he is making an effort to bond with the family
reading3: he wants career advice or a job introduction

scenario: My long-distance partner's calls have become shorter, and last week he missed our usual Sunday call and explained it with 'busy day'.
reading1: something is wrong in his life that he has not told me about
reading2: he is losing interest in the relationship
reading3: his schedule has become demanding and he is tired

scenario: A friend repeatedly asks me to join her at events but then spends most of the evening with other people. Afterwards she thanks me warmly for coming.
reading1: she uses me as a safe companion to arrive with but does not care to spend time with me
reading2: she wants me to meet her other friends so that we all become closer
reading3: she wants my company and is trying to be a good host to everyone

scenario: Our friend group's yearly trip is being planned in a chat I was not added to. I learned about it from a casual remark.
reading1: the plan is still only between two people and the wider chat does not exist yet
reading2: I was left off by mistake and they will add me when it is noticed
reading3: they deliberately did not include me

scenario: For about six months I have dreaded Monday mornings in a job I once chose deliberately. I still do the work well, and colleagues say I seem fine.
reading1: I have outgrown this field and need a different direction
reading2: this is a temporary slump caused by my current team or workload and will pass
reading3: I am burned out and need rest and better boundaries, not a new career

scenario: I recently stopped enjoying a hobby I did for ten years. I still show up out of habit, but I no longer look forward to it.
reading1: I have been doing it in a way that stopped being fun, and a change in how I do it would help
reading2: I am low or tired in general and the hobby is just one place where it shows
reading3: I have simply grown out of it and should let it go

scenario: At family gatherings I increasingly feel like an observer rather than a member. Nobody has done anything to exclude me, and I used to enjoy these events.
reading1: I am dealing with stress or low mood that is making me withdraw from everything
reading2: the gatherings themselves have changed, with new people and topics, and the distance is not about me
reading3: I have changed and my values have moved away from my family's

scenario: I keep comparing my career to my college friends', and I feel I am behind. None of them has said anything about my progress.
reading1: I am genuinely behind and need to change something concrete
reading2: I want something different from what they have and am confusing that with falling behind
reading3: I am measuring myself against a highlight reel and I am doing fine for my own path

scenario: I've felt a strong urge to move to a different city, even though my life here is stable and I have no specific reason to leave.
reading1: I need a fresh start because I have outgrown my current life here
reading2: I am restless because of something in my life here that I haven't looked at, and moving would not fix it
reading3: it is a passing fantasy triggered by seeing others' travels and not a real need

scenario: I laughed at a joke about my hometown's culture and then felt a stab of discomfort I could not explain. It has stayed with me for days.
reading1: I was simply tired or in a sensitive mood and it would have passed with any joke
reading2: I am uncomfortable with how I have distanced myself from where I am from
reading3: I feel more loyalty to my background than I realised

scenario: I got the grades I was aiming for, and instead of feeling proud I feel flat and a little lost.
reading1: I am exhausted after long stress and the flatness is a normal crash
reading2: I was chasing a goal that was never really mine, and I need to find my own
reading3: I need a new goal to focus on, and the flatness will lift once I have one

scenario: When people ask what I do, I notice I downplay my work and change the subject. I am not embarrassed by the job, as far as I know.
reading1: I fear being judged by people who have more prestigious careers
reading2: I do not really identify with my work any more
reading3: I am naturally private and I do this about many things, not just work

scenario: I notice that around my old friends I act in ways that feel like an earlier version of me, and afterwards I feel drained.
reading1: I am tired in general and social effort drains me regardless of who I am with
reading2: I am slipping into old roles out of habit, and could change how I behave with them
reading3: I have genuinely changed and these friendships no longer fit who I am

scenario: I've been reading and thinking a lot about a religion I was not raised in. I am drawn to it but also feel guilty about my own tradition.
reading1: I am looking for community or structure and the religion is just the vehicle
reading2: I am curious intellectually and it is not a real change in my beliefs
reading3: I am genuinely moving toward a new spiritual path

scenario: I suddenly feel envious when I see friends having children, though I had always said I did not want any.
reading1: I am envious of the life stage and attention, not of parenthood itself
reading2: I have changed my mind about wanting a family
reading3: I am reacting to social pressure and I still do not want children

scenario: After a year abroad I came back feeling like a stranger in my own home town, with everyone treating me as if nothing had changed.
reading1: this is ordinary reverse culture shock and will fade within months
reading2: my friends and family are right and I am the one who has been exaggerating the change
reading3: I have changed a lot and my home no longer fits me

scenario: I keep saying yes to every request at work and at home, and I resent it. When I try to say no, I feel anxious and selfish.
reading1: I need to learn to set boundaries and the anxiety will lessen with practice
reading2: I have too many commitments and need to restructure my workload, not just refuse
reading3: my sense of worth is tied to being needed, and that is the deeper issue

scenario: I am thinking about changing my name to something that feels more like me. My family is likely to be hurt by it.
reading1: I am looking for a symbolic fresh start because of something else in my life
reading2: it is a deep and lasting need and I should go ahead
reading3: it is a passing mood and I will not want it in a year

scenario: I feel I do not belong in my university course, although my grades are good. My classmates all seem more passionate than I am.
reading1: I have impostor feelings that do not reflect the facts
reading2: I chose the wrong subject and should switch
reading3: I am less outwardly enthusiastic, not less committed, and I fit just fine

scenario: I used to be the funny one in my friend group. Lately I have gone quiet in company and do not feel like performing.
reading1: I have stopped wanting to play that role and I am becoming a different person
reading2: I am just in a thoughtful phase and my humour will return on its own
reading3: I am going through a low mood that is dulling my usual energy

scenario: I got an offer from an impressive company, and rather than feeling excited I felt relief mixed with dread.
reading1: I am relieved to have security and the dread is only normal change anxiety
reading2: I am afraid of failing in a bigger role, but the job is right for me
reading3: I do not actually want this career path

scenario: People keep telling me I would be a good teacher. I find myself thinking about it often, but I am an engineer by training and have never taught.
reading1: I have a real calling to teach and should explore it
reading2: I enjoy the praise and the image, not the actual work of teaching
reading3: I want more meaning in my work, and teaching is only one possible form of that

scenario: I realised I have not felt truly proud of anything I have done in months, even objectively good things.
reading1: I have been doing things I do not value, so success does not register
reading2: my standards have become unrealistically high
reading3: I am mildly depressed and positive feelings are muted

scenario: I notice that I keep rehearsing a conversation with my father in my head, one where I finally tell him how his expectations affected me.
reading1: I have already moved past it and the rehearsal is a habit of mind, not a need
reading2: I need to process the feelings on my own or with a therapist before I talk to him
reading3: I need to have this conversation in real life and I am ready

scenario: I am drawn to a creative project I abandoned as a teenager, and I keep imagining going back to it, but I feel foolish at my age.
reading1: I am nostalgic for an earlier time more than for the project itself
reading2: I want a creative outlet in general, and this project is just the first idea that came
reading3: I should take it seriously because it is a genuine part of me

scenario: When my friends talk about their five-year plans, I feel nothing and have no plan of my own. Others say it must be freeing, but it feels empty.
reading1: I am unmotivated because I have not found what matters to me yet
reading2: I prefer to live flexibly and the emptiness is just a reaction to other people's expectations
reading3: I am deflated or low and would feel differently when I recover

scenario: I've started getting irritated at my partner's habits that I used to find endearing, and I am unsure whether that says something about them or me.
reading1: I am going through a phase of wanting more independence
reading2: I am under general stress and it spills onto whoever is closest
reading3: the relationship is slowly wearing down and the irritation is a sign

scenario: After a big win, I felt the urge to quit something I had worked towards for years, as if I had proved what I needed to.
reading1: the urge is a post-achievement dip that will pass
reading2: I am afraid of the pressure that comes with continued success
reading3: I have achieved what I wanted and it is time to move on

scenario: I hesitate before telling people about my interests, because they might seem odd. I have mostly stopped bringing them up.
reading1: I am afraid of being judged and have been suppressing parts of myself
reading2: my interests really are niche and I am fine with keeping them private
reading3: I have not met the right people and it is a question of finding the right community

scenario: I find myself drawn to the lifestyle of friends who left conventional careers. I admire them, but I also feel anxious thinking about doing the same.
reading1: I want more autonomy in my current job and do not need a complete career break
reading2: I admire the story more than the reality, and I would not like it in practice
reading3: I really want that kind of life and the anxiety is only fear of change

scenario: I regularly find I agree with whoever I last spoke to, then feel confused about what I actually think.
reading1: I am avoiding conflict by agreeing and I do have views, just not expressed ones
reading2: I have a weak sense of my own views and need time to develop them
reading3: I am open-minded and persuadable, and this is a healthy trait that just feels disorienting

scenario: I was proud to be accepted to a competitive programme, but now that I am here I feel I do not deserve it and expect to be 'found out'.
reading1: I am experiencing impostor feelings and my performance is fine
reading2: this programme genuinely is above my level and I need to adapt quickly
reading3: I do not actually want to be here and am looking for a reason to leave

scenario: I have been told I am 'too sensitive' my entire life, and recently I began to wonder whether it is a weakness or just who I am.
reading1: others have been unfair and my sensitivity is no more than normal
reading2: it is a trait that comes with real strengths and I should stop apologising for it
reading3: I have an anxiety pattern that I could work on rather than accept

scenario: I recently turned thirty and keep feeling I should have a clear 'direction' by now, though I am not unhappy day to day.
reading1: I actually do want more structure and a clear aim in my life
reading2: this is an age milestone reaction that will fade after a few weeks
reading3: the pressure comes from outside expectations and I am doing fine

scenario: I have felt unusually restless for a month and cannot say why. My routines are unchanged and nothing dramatic has happened.
reading1: it is a temporary restlessness with no meaning behind it
reading2: I am low on sleep, exercise or stimulation and need a physical reset
reading3: something in my life needs changing, even if I cannot name it yet

scenario: I am an immigrant and recently found myself slipping into my first language when I am emotional, which I never used to do.
reading1: it is a normal quirk of bilingual people under emotion and means nothing special
reading2: I am reconnecting with a part of my identity I had pushed down
reading3: I am homesick and stressed and my first language is comforting

scenario: I took a personality test at work and the results described someone I do not recognise. I cannot decide if the test is wrong or I do not know myself.
reading1: the test is unreliable and the description is not me
reading2: I do not know myself as well as I thought
reading3: the test describes a work version of me, not the whole person

scenario: A stranger told me I 'seemed very guarded', and it has been in my head for a week.
reading1: it is true and I have built walls that I should examine
reading2: it was a single remark based on a brief encounter and says nothing about me
reading3: I am guarded in specific situations for good reasons and that is not a problem

scenario: I find myself rereading my old journals, and the person I was five years ago seems braver than I am now.
reading1: I have grown more careful for good reasons, and that is not a loss
reading2: I have lost something important and want it back
reading3: I am romanticising my past and the old me had the same doubts

scenario: Lately I take much longer to make simple decisions, like what to order or what to wear, and I feel a bit paralysed.
reading1: I am just tired and it will pass with rest
reading2: I am anxious or overwhelmed and it shows in small choices
reading3: I fear making wrong choices because of bigger decisions I am avoiding

scenario: I got invited to speak at an event about my background and field. I said yes quickly, then felt uneasy about being seen as a representative of a group.
reading1: I do not want to be defined by that part of my identity in public
reading2: I feel responsibility to do it well for others and the unease is a sign I care about it
reading3: I am nervous about public speaking, and the representation issue is a cover for that

scenario: My roommate and I used to chat for hours in the kitchen every evening, but lately, they retreat to their room the moment they get home. When we do pass in the hallway, they give me a brief nod but avoid starting a conversation. They haven't brought up any issues regarding our living arrangement.
reading1: they are upset with me about something I did
reading2: they are going through a difficult personal period and need more solitude
reading3: they are preparing to move out and are starting to emotionally detach

scenario: My manager used to join our weekly project syncs to provide direct guidance, but for the past month, they have sent a brief video update instead. They have also stopped responding to my follow-up questions in the project chat. This change occurred without any prior warning or explanation.
reading1: they are trying to grant me more autonomy to prove I can lead the project independently
reading2: they are losing confidence in my ability and are distancing themselves to avoid providing feedback
reading3: they are overwhelmed by a new, high-priority project and are minimizing their time spent in meetings

scenario: For the past month, my partner has become unusually calm and has stopped bringing up any of the household grievances we used to discuss. They are spending much more time alone in the garden than usual. While they are pleasant during our brief interactions, they seem much more detached from our usual evening debates.
reading1: they have reached a new level of emotional maturity and are choosing to let small things go
reading2: they have emotionally checked out of our relationship and are distancing themselves
reading3: they are privately managing a significant stressor and are using solitude to cope
